items.title: Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2022
items.q: he was following the advice of Milhaud saying the same thing about when you travel open your ears, incorporate music you hear in other countries into what you’re doing

ctx.x: Yeah and I guess socially the implication is like okay we’re going from a drab world to the world’s opening up and the colors are opening and Jackson Pollock’s throwing paint. And you know the whole thing happened in that time period that really revolutionized the future, and even the acceptance of the Beatles and all that. There was a lot of groundwork that was laid.

Then Dave in his older years would say, “When I look back at it I guess in a way I was kind of a pioneer of world music.” You know the stuff that came back from that tour that made it into jazz. And of course he was following the advice of Milhaud saying the same thing about when you travel open your ears, incorporate music you hear in other countries into what you’re doing and then you’ll be an innovator helping your art form grow.

I’ve had the privilege of being in the Brubeck house twice to interview your parents. And I was struck, Dave had been working on a piece the day I got there and he took me to the piano and he said come on. It was for piano and voice, and the war in Afghanistan had just started and it was reflective of that. And it was interesting because he said, “Iola said no one will want to sing it. It’s too sad.” And I got this little picture of their back and forth and her opinions, voicing her opinions about his music, in…
